2 · Paste the post copy

Alaska's planned second power line would end at Healy, south of Clear and Eielson, where the Air Force offered land for AI data centers.

It would run about 223 miles from Beluga through West Susitna and Willow.

Clear, Eielson and JBER hold the 12 parcels offered this spring. Lisa Murkowski told the American Homefront Project she isn't a proponent of data centers there because of "an insecure energy base at this time."

The Energy Department intends up to $150 million, citing the military and mining.

The wire is still in planning. The land had no award by late September. No record behind the wire says data center.

Today's intertie, the new wire's stops and money, three bases and Murkowski's sentence, then five records, two saying data center.

Why is the record for a Defense Production Act line silent on data centers offered for Railbelt bases?

#Railbelt #BelugaHealy #AlaskaGrid

3 · Post, then paste this as the FIRST comment (within a minute)
